html:
SMTO-AUT-0011 — The sign-in link or code expired before it was used

GUID: 1b1b508e-e537-5f81-8e3f-0666c981c981
Slug: auth-transaction-expired
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • The sign-in link, device code, or short-term access SMTO had for this step is no longer valid, usually because it took too long or the connection's settings changed. Old links can't be reused.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close old sign-in tabs. If the step was making a change, check first whether it already happened. Then ask SMTO to try the step again for a new Open authorization page link or Device code. Each sign-in link or code works only once and for a limited time, so only a new one will work.
  2. Finish signing in straight away: browser links last at most 10 minutes and device codes at most 30 minutes. SMTO cancels unfinished sign-ins after that time so old links can't be misused.
  3. Don't edit this connection in Parameter Store while the Task is using it. Changing the connection's settings cancels any access SMTO was holding for this step.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in page says Authorization complete, and the step continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't reuse an old sign-in link, and don't paste sign-in codes or passwords into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An OAuth browser or device transaction expired before completion, or an operation-bound credential lease is missing, expired, or bound to a different run, profile revision or Gateway.

What this means

  • A browser/device transaction expired, or a token lease is missing or bound to different current authority. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • A browser/device transaction expired, or a token lease is missing or bound to different current authority.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify transaction expiry versus lease-binding mismatch and inspect the current pending connection.

How to fix it

  • Restart authorization from the waiting operation to create a new transaction (browser links last at most 10 minutes, device codes at most 30), or let the broker issue a fresh lease (at most 10 minutes, bound to the exact connection and client revisions, run, operation and Gateway). Avoid editing the connection or client records mid-operation, and never reuse an old launch link or callback.
  • Restart the current authorization flow or obtain a fresh operation-bound lease through the supported broker.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh transaction or lease is valid for the exact current connection and operation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
